added_provisions.reason: The M078-Q01 gold answer states twice that fraud or collusion in securing the prior registration defeats the priority obtained, and claim CL-M078-Q01-006 asserts it as a rule. No provision entry in the researcher's map carried section 7(2) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance: PROV-M078-001 is section 7(1) and PROV-M078-002 is section 7(4). Section 7(2) was added as a verified provision with a checked verbatim excerpt, put in M078-Q01's supporting set with an excepts edge to PROV-M078-001, and cited by claims CL-M078-Q01-006 and CL-M078-Q01-012, so the claim is no longer unsupported.

question_decisions.note: Every indispensable provision (PROV-M078-001, -003, -005, -007) verifies on wording and applies at 2020-04; PROV-M078-007 is partially_verified on its temporal note only, which does not block. Sections 7, 8, 14, 27 and 30 are untouched by every Registration of Documents amendment Act in the corpus that predates April 2020, and the one post-date amendment to section 8 (18-2024 s.2) was correctly excluded. The one unsupported claim, on fraud and collusion, is fixed by the added PROV-M078-901. Priority as between a lease and a mortgage bond is settled by the register alone, so statute_only stands; an independent search for an alternative Act returned only the statutory charges in the housing and State Mortgage Bank statutes, which do not apply to a private lender, confirming the researcher's negative result. The answer being given on two footings, registered lease and unregistered lease, is left as it stands but is raised for the lawyer.

Block confirmed independently. Section 3(1) of Act No. 12 of 2006 leaves the rate to a Ministerial Order in the Gazette and no Order, Schedule or rate table is in the corpus. The obvious alternative, the Stamp Duty Act No. 43 of 1982, does not help: its section 2 also charges duty at the prescribed rate and the corpus carries no Schedule to it. Sections 4(g) and 3(1) and the exclusion of the provincial charge all verify, so only the money figure is missing.

All five indispensable provisions (PROV-M078-011, -012, -013, -014, -015) verify on wording, role and temporal position; sections 6 and 8 of Act No. 12 of 2006 carry only the 2008 amendments, twelve years before the matter date. Reading the whole of section 6 confirms that no paragraph, including (dd) and (ddd), names a bond or mortgage, so the residual limb (e) is right. Section 14 confirms the Commissioner-General reading in PROV-M078-018, and section 37 of the Western Province Financial Statute reaches only transfers, court documents and motor vehicle transfers, so the provincial route is properly excluded. The only soft point is the supporting notary rule (6), which is partially_verified on temporal grounds and is not indispensable.

disagreements.researcher_position: Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance is marked applicable_to_matter_date=false and recorded as a corpus gap, because the corpus carries the text as amended by Act No. 30 of 2022 and Act No. 4 of 2024 and the April 2020 wording is said not to be in the corpus.
disagreements.verifier_position: Both amending Acts are in the corpus and neither touches the words excerpted at PROV-M078-009. 30-2022 s.2 repealed only from the words shall be of force to the end of the section; 4-2024 s.2 renumbered the section, replaced paragraphs (a) and (b) of the renumbered subsection (1) and added subsection (2). The excerpted opening words stood in April 2020, so the provision is applicable and this is not a corpus gap. The boolean field was left untouched because it is outside what the verifier may edit; the correction is recorded in the verifier_note and corpus_gaps.

disagreements.researcher_position: The Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982 was set aside in full because section 13 of Act No. 12 of 2006 displaces it for instruments other than transfers of immovable property, motor vehicles and court documents.
disagreements.verifier_position: Section 13 displaces the 1982 Act only in so far as it is inconsistent with the 2006 Act. Section 16 of the 1982 Act, on how a bond or mortgage for money to be lent is charged where the amount secured is limited or unlimited, has no counterpart in the 2006 Act and speaks directly to the mode of calculation that M078-Q03 asks for. Whether it survives is a legal judgement, not a corpus question. It does not unblock M078-Q03, because the 1982 Act also charges duty only at the prescribed rate and no rate table is in the corpus.

disagreements.researcher_position: Sections 27 and 30 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance were inserted by section 4 of the Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 1958.
disagreements.verifier_position: 22-1958 s.4 substituted a heading in Chapter V of the principal enactment and inserted no section. The bracketed marker the corpus prints against sections 27 and 30 is that heading marker. Both sections are recorded as in force from 1927 with no amendment event, which is the sound basis for applying them at 2020-04, so the conclusion is unaffected but the stated reason is wrong.

unsupported_claims: CL-M078-Q01-006 asserted that under s.7(2) fraud or collusion in securing the prior registration defeats the priority so obtained, but cited only PROV-M078-001 (s.7(1)) and PROV-M078-002 (s.7(4)), neither of which contains those words. Fixed by adding PROV-M078-901 (s.7(2)) and citing it from CL-M078-Q01-006 and CL-M078-Q01-012.

PROV-M078-014's why_relevant relies on duty not being compounded under s.7 of Act No. 12 of 2006, and the M078-Q04 gold answer opens the s.8(1) rule the same way, but no provision entry carries s.7. Not fixed by adding a provision: s.7(1) reaches insurance policies, licences, credit card claims, large employers and categories the Commissioner-General permits, none of which covers a private mortgage bond, so the qualification is inert on these facts.

The M078-Q01 conclusion advises Kamal Perera to take the matter up with the lessee if the lease is already registered. The corpus holds nothing on subordination, postponement or a lessee's concurrence, so that limb is practical advice rather than a statute-supported claim. It is not asserted as a claim in answer_claims, so no claim was rejected, but the lawyer should confirm the prose.
temporal_issues: PROV-M078-006 and PROV-M078-007 misattribute sections 27 and 30 to insertion by 22-1958 s.4, which in fact substituted a Chapter V heading. Both marked partially_verified; applicability at 2020-04 is unaffected.

PROV-M078-020 asserts that the rule (6) wording substituted by 31-2022 s.16(4) is word for word the same as the wording it replaced. The amending Act does not set out the replaced words and the pre-2022 text is not in the corpus, so this is not checkable here. Marked partially_verified; the provision is supporting only for M078-Q04.

PROV-M078-009 is flagged not applicable to the matter date on a reading of the 2022 and 2024 amendments that the amending Acts in the corpus do not bear out. Marked partially_verified with the correction stated.

Checked and found sound: no Registration of Documents amendment Act in the corpus that predates April 2020 (22-1958, 27-1969, 4-1974, 14-1974, 19-1976, 50-1982, 5-1990, 48-2011, 21-2013) touches sections 7, 8, 14, 27 or 30, and the post-date 18-2024 s.2 amendment to section 8 was correctly excluded. Sections 6 and 8 of Act No. 12 of 2006 carry only the 10-2008 amendments. Rule (17)(a) of Notaries Ordinance s.31 was untouched by 31-2022 s.16(10) and 6-2024 s.3(6), which reached only paragraph (b), sub-paragraph (b)(iii) and paragraph (c).
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Section 7(2) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance was missing and has been added as PROV-M078-901.

The proviso to rule (17) of Notaries Ordinance s.31 lets the parties authorise the notary in writing to dispense with the search, in which case the notary need only write the reference to the previous registration at the head of the deed. The M078-Q01 answer presents the search as unqualified. Not fatal, since a lender's notary would not be so authorised on these facts, but the lawyer should note it.
Section 43-1982/s16 on how a bond or mortgage is charged: see the disagreement above.

The term prescribed bank in 12-2006 s.8(2) is not defined in the Act's interpretation section (s.14) and depends on regulations under s.12 that are not in the corpus. The M078-Q04 answer does not name a bank, so nothing turns on it, but the procedure cannot be described more concretely from the corpus.
12-2006 s.11 applies the Inland Revenue Act to this Act. It is not cited and would round out the recovery limb of the M078-Q04 procedure, but it is not indispensable.
case_law_dependence: None found. No gold answer cites a case, a law report or a judicial doctrine, and the validator's case-law regex is clean. All three questions turn on statutory text that the corpus holds in full.
enrichment_issues: None. All three Tier A questions are classified keep and enrichment.applied is false on each, with no added facts, which is what the classification requires.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: PROV-M078-001 and PROV-M078-002 both point at 23-1927/s7, and PROV-M078-012, -013 both at 12-2006/s6, and PROV-M078-014 through -017 all at 12-2006/s8. These are distinct subsections, not duplicates, and the added PROV-M078-901 follows the same pattern for s.7(2).
No background leaks a statute name, section number or conclusion, because no enrichment was applied.

lawyer_questions: M078-Q01 is answered on two footings because the scenario never says whether the Indenture of Lease was registered, and the corpus holds nothing on how a registered lessee's priority can be subordinated or waived. Should the question stay proposed_gold with a branching gold answer, or be reclassified blocked_scenario_ambiguity so that a single determinate gold can be written once the lawyer fixes the missing fact?

Does section 13 of the Stamp Duty (Special Provisions) Act, No. 12 of 2006 leave section 16 of the Stamp Duty Act, No. 43 of 1982 in force for calculating duty on a mortgage bond, given that section 13 displaces the 1982 Act only in so far as it is inconsistent?

M078-Q01 does not state the term of the lease. Proviso (xi) to section 8 excludes only a tenancy at will, a tenancy for a month or less, or one determinable on a month's notice. Is the examiner's assumption that an Indenture of Lease of a house is necessarily outside that proviso safe enough to state as a rule in the gold answer?

Section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance: confirm the verifier's reading that the 2022 and 2024 amendments left the opening words untouched, so PROV-M078-009 was in force in April 2020 and the corpus gap recorded against it should be withdrawn.

M078-Q04 concludes that the duty is payable to a prescribed bank and administered by the Commissioner-General rather than to the Western Provincial Council, on the footing that section 37 of the Western Province Financial Statute does not charge mortgage bonds. Confirm that this matches practice in April 2020, since paragraph (a) of the corpus text of section 37 is garbled.
